recognize_zh: 組織切片中可見多個圓形「花冠狀」構造：中央膨大的囊泡（vesicle）周圍放射狀排列瓶梗（phialides），外緣堆滿成串的小圓形分生孢子（conidia），背景也布滿散落孢子，這是麴菌（Aspergillus）分生孢子頭的典型外觀，常見於暴露於空氣的腔室如鼻竇。
features: Multiple radiate conidial heads with a central swollen vesicle
Phialides arranged radially around the vesicle, forming a sunburst pattern
Dense rims and sheets of small round brown conidia at the periphery and in the background
Conidiophore stalk sections visible at the center of some heads
Fungal ball-like aggregate without identifiable host tissue in this field; tan-brown tinted H&E
describe_en: Section of nasal cavity material shows a fungal aggregate composed of sheets of small round conidia and several well-formed conidial heads. Each head consists of a swollen central vesicle with radially arranged phialides bearing chains of conidia, producing a sunburst appearance. Host tissue and tissue invasion are not evaluable in this field. The fruiting bodies are characteristic of Aspergillus species, a form typically produced in air-exposed cavities such as the paranasal sinuses; fungal culture is needed for species identification.

ddx.vs: Mucorales show broad, ribbon-like, pauci-septate hyphae with right-angle branching and sporangia with a columella rather than radiate conidial heads with phialides.
Penicillium forms brush-like (penicillate) branched conidiophores without a swollen vesicle.
Fusarium has acute-angle septate hyphae like Aspergillus but does not form vesicular conidial heads and produces banana-shaped macroconidia in culture.
